chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who stole a cluster of dates from an orchard, its value being two dirhams, he said: “The hand is cut off for it.”

key_terms.بُسْتَانٍ: an orchard or garden from which the item was stolen
key_terms.دِرْهَمَانِ: two dirhams, indicating the assessed amount
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the hand is cut off; the hadd punishment is applied

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stealing property worth two dirhams in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft when the stolen property reaches a specified value. Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that stealing a date cluster worth two dirhams incurs the hadd punishment of amputation.
